chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray the two rak'ahs of the morning prayer, which is Fajr, when the dawn had appeared and shone brightly.

key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: Dawn (specifically referring to the time of the morning prayer)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الصُّبْحِ: The two rak'ahs of the morning prayer

ai.seo_question: When should the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr be prayed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurarah, clarifies the specific temporal window for the Sunnah of Fajr, distinguishing the 'true dawn' (al-fajr al-sadiq) from the 'false dawn' (al-fajr al-kadhib). In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is critical for ensuring the prayer is performed within its valid time before the obligatory Fajr prayer begins, reflecting the precision with which the Ahl al-Bayt defined ritual timings.
